raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year's plan for my little piece of land.

---

My plot is only 1.1 mu — really just a strip. My husband works away from home most of the year, my child is grown and in the city, so it's mostly me handling this land. Thirty years I've been doing wheat-maize on this ground, so I pretty much know what it needs.

**Wheat** went in last October, around the 10th. I always use the regular commercial variety from the ag supply shop — the kind everyone around here plants. No sense trying anything fancy on 1.1 mu; if it fails I've got no backup. Before planting I put down about 40 kg of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) as base, and then in spring at jointing I'll topdress about 20 kg of urea per mu. That gives me roughly 15 kg of pure N per mu total — the technician at the township station used to say 14 or 15 is right, and my own experience lines up with that. I used to put on a bit more urea but I noticed the wheat fell over in a wet year, so I pulled back.

Irrigation is three times for wheat — once in winter before the ground freezes hard, once at jointing right after I topdress, and once at grain filling. The well is metered and it costs me, but wheat without the jointing water will lose yield and I saw that happen to a neighbor in a dry spring. I also spray herbicide once in spring for the weeds, and if I see aphids I'll do one round of insecticide. My sprayer is the old hand-pump one — fine for 1.1 mu.

After wheat harvest in early June, I turn right around and plant **maize**, same week if possible. No time for real tillage — I hire the direct-seed planter (the machine guy comes through the village), he plants straight into the wheat stubble. Seed is hybrid, whatever the shop has — usually something like Zhengdan 958 or the newer ones they push. Base fertilizer at planting, about 30 kg of compound, and then one topdress of urea (maybe 15 kg) around the big trumpet stage. Maize mostly gets rain in summer so usually only one irrigation, sometimes none if July is wet. Herbicide once after emergence, pests I mostly let go — I'm not spraying if I don't see damage.

For both crops I pay the machine operators — rotary tiller before wheat, the drill, the combine for harvest. Can't justify owning equipment for this much land. Labor is just me, my husband helps when he's home on weekends.

I'm expecting around 430 kg/mu for wheat and 480 for maize — that's what I usually get. Nothing special, but steady. My total input spending is maybe 700 yuan for the whole year across both crops, which is what I can manage. Grain prices aren't great, but this land mostly feeds us and the surplus gives some pocket money. If I was doing this for income alone I wouldn't bother with 1.1 mu — but it's family land and I'm not going to let it sit.
